title: Rav Kahana son of Rav Chinena the Elder
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Pesachim 76b: “He recited a baraita: Bread that was baked,” etc. Seder HaDorot cites from Yuchasin that he was Shmuel’s student and writes on this, “I have not found it.” Hyman considers Seder HaDorot’s quotation inaccurate, for Yuchasin cites only “Rav Kahana bar Chinena, Shmuel’s student”; Hyman interprets this as referring to Rav Chinena his father, who was Shmuel’s student, as is always its way; he notes Rav Chinena bar Kahana, who always spoke in Shmuel’s name, as explained in his entry. But Rav Kahana son of Rav Chinena the Elder is a different Amora, for Rav Chinena the Elder was Rabbi Assi’s student, as in Pesachim 75a.
Yuchasin HaShalem cites “Rav Kahana bar Chinena, Rav Kahana son of Rav Chinena the Elder,” and Yuchasin’s reading in Pesachim 76b was like Dikdukei Soferim’s: Rav Kahana son of Rav Chinena.

notes.text: תני is a baraita-reciter role. Hyman’s interpretation of which father was Shmuel’s student, always claims and distinct Chinena/Kahana orderings remain attributed, not automatically reconciled.

Pesachim 76b directly names Kahana son of Chinena the Elder as reciter. Hyman’s Yuchasin interpretation, father/student relationship and always claim are retained without independent validation of that exact edition.
